chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Samaanah said:

I asked him about a man who sells food or fruit which he had purchased but had not yet taken possession of. He said: 'No [it is not valid], until he takes possession of it, unless there are with him people with whom he shares [ownership], so one of them takes out his share from his partnership with profit, or one of them appoints him [as an agent], so there is no objection.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell food or fruit before taking physical possession of it?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the conditions for the validity of selling unpossessed goods (bay' al-madmun), a key topic in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the transfer of risk and ownership. It distinguishes between a simple sale, which requires physical possession (qabd), and permissible exceptions in partnership (shirakah) or agency (wilayah), where the seller disposes of a share or delegates the right to sell without full possession. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on actual control over the commodity to prevent uncertainty (gharar) in commercial transactions.
